text: All that we are is the result of what we have thought: it is founded on our thoughts, it is made up of our thoughts.
source: Dhammapada 1 (tr. F. Max Müller, 1881, public domain)

text: For hatred does not cease by hatred at any time: hatred ceases by love, this is an old rule.
source: Dhammapada 5 (tr. F. Max Müller, 1881, public domain)

text: Earnestness is the path of immortality, thoughtlessness the path of death. Those who are in earnest do not die, those who are thoughtless are as if dead already.
source: Dhammapada 21 (tr. F. Max Müller, 1881, public domain)

text: As a fletcher makes straight his arrow, a wise man makes straight his trembling and unsteady thought, which is difficult to guard, difficult to hold back.
source: Dhammapada 33 (tr. F. Max Müller, 1881, public domain)

text: Not the perversities of others, not their sins of commission or omission, but his own misdeeds and negligences should a sage take notice of.
source: Dhammapada 50 (tr. F. Max Müller, 1881, public domain)

text: Like a beautiful flower, full of colour, but without scent, are the fine but fruitless words of him who does not act accordingly.
source: Dhammapada 51 (tr. F. Max Müller, 1881, public domain)

text: The scent of flowers does not travel against the wind, nor that of sandal-wood, or of Tagara and Mallika flowers; but the odour of good people travels even against the wind; a good man pervades every place.
source: Dhammapada 54 (tr. F. Max Müller, 1881, public domain)

text: The fool who knows his foolishness, is wise at least so far. But a fool who thinks himself wise, he is called a fool indeed.
source: Dhammapada 63 (tr. F. Max Müller, 1881, public domain)

text: As long as the evil deed done does not bear fruit, the fool thinks it is like honey; but when it ripens, then the fool suffers grief.
source: Dhammapada 69 (tr. F. Max Müller, 1881, public domain)

text: Well-makers lead the water wherever they like; fletchers bend the arrow; carpenters bend a log of wood; wise people fashion themselves.
source: Dhammapada 80 (tr. F. Max Müller, 1881, public domain)

text: As a solid rock is not shaken by the wind, wise people falter not amidst blame and praise.
source: Dhammapada 81 (tr. F. Max Müller, 1881, public domain)

text: Let no man think lightly of evil, saying in his heart, It will not come nigh unto me. Even by the falling of water-drops a water-pot is filled; the fool becomes full of evil, even if he gather it little by little.
source: Dhammapada 121 (tr. F. Max Müller, 1881, public domain)

text: He who has no wound on his hand, may touch poison with his hand; poison does not affect one who has no wound; nor is there evil for one who does not commit evil.
source: Dhammapada 124 (tr. F. Max Müller, 1881, public domain)

text: By oneself the evil is done, by oneself one suffers; by oneself evil is left undone, by oneself one is purified. Purity and impurity belong to oneself, no one can purify another.
source: Dhammapada 165 (tr. F. Max Müller, 1881, public domain)

text: Let a man overcome anger by love, let him overcome evil by good; let him overcome the greedy by liberality, the liar by truth!
source: Dhammapada 223 (tr. F. Max Müller, 1881, public domain)

text: The fault of others is easily perceived, but that of oneself is difficult to perceive; a man winnows his neighbour's faults like chaff, but his own fault he hides, as a cheat hides the bad die from the gambler.
source: Dhammapada 252 (tr. F. Max Müller, 1881, public domain)

text: Is it not pleasant to learn with a constant perseverance and application?
cjk: 子曰：「學而時習之，不亦說乎？」

text: I daily examine myself on three points: whether, in transacting business for others, I may have been not faithful; whether, in intercourse with friends, I may have been not sincere; whether I may have not mastered and practised the instructions of my teacher.
cjk: 曾子曰：「吾日三省吾身：為人謀而不忠乎？與朋友交而不信乎？傳不習乎？」

text: When you have faults, do not fear to abandon them.
cjk: 過則勿憚改。

text: I will not be afflicted at men's not knowing me; I will be afflicted that I do not know men.
cjk: 子曰：「不患人之不己知，患不知人也。」

text: At fifteen, I had my mind bent on learning. At thirty, I stood firm. At forty, I had no doubts. At fifty, I knew the decrees of Heaven. At sixty, my ear was an obedient organ for the reception of truth. At seventy, I could follow what my heart desired, without transgressing what was right.
cjk: 子曰：「吾十有五而志于學，三十而立，四十而不惑，五十而知天命，六十而耳順，七十而從心所欲，不踰矩。」

text: If a man keeps cherishing his old knowledge, so as continually to be acquiring new, he may be a teacher of others.
cjk: 子曰：「溫故而知新，可以為師矣。」

text: Learning without thought is labour lost; thought without learning is perilous.
cjk: 子曰：「學而不思則罔，思而不學則殆。」

text: When you know a thing, to hold that you know it; and when you do not know a thing, to allow that you do not know it; this is knowledge.
cjk: 子曰：「由！誨女知之乎？知之為知之，不知為不知，是知也。」

text: If a man in the morning hear the right way, he may die in the evening without regret.
cjk: 子曰：「朝聞道，夕死可矣。」

text: I am not concerned that I have no place, I am concerned how I may fit myself for one. I am not concerned that I am not known, I seek to be worthy to be known.
cjk: 子曰：「不患無位，患所以立。不患莫己知，求為可知也。」

text: When we see men of worth, we should think of equalling them; when we see men of a contrary character, we should turn inwards and examine ourselves.
cjk: 子曰：「見賢思齊焉，見不賢而內自省也。」

text: Virtue is not left to stand alone. He who practises it will have neighbors.
cjk: 子曰：「德不孤，必有鄰。」

text: They who know the truth are not equal to those who love it, and they who love it are not equal to those who delight in it.
source: Analects 6:18 in Legge's numbering (tr. James Legge, 1893, public domain)
cjk: 子曰：「知之者不如好之者，好之者不如樂之者。」

text: When I have presented one corner of a subject to any one, and he cannot from it learn the other three, I do not repeat my lesson.
cjk: 子曰：「不憤不啟，不悱不發，舉一隅不以三隅反，則不復也。」

text: With coarse rice to eat, with water to drink, and my bended arm for a pillow; I have still joy in the midst of these things. Riches and honours acquired by unrighteousness, are to me as a floating cloud.
source: Analects 7:15 in Legge's numbering (tr. James Legge, 1893, public domain)
cjk: 子曰：「飯疏食飲水，曲肱而枕之，樂亦在其中矣。不義而富且貴，於我如浮雲。」

text: When I walk along with two others, they may serve me as my teachers. I will select their good qualities and follow them, their bad qualities and avoid them.
source: Analects 7:21 in Legge's numbering (tr. James Legge, 1893, public domain)
cjk: 子曰：「三人行，必有我師焉。擇其善者而從之，其不善者而改之。」

text: It passes on just like this, not ceasing day or night!
attribution: Confucius, standing by a stream, Analects 9:16
source: Analects 9:16 in Legge's numbering (tr. James Legge, 1893, public domain)
cjk: 子在川上曰：「逝者如斯夫！不舍晝夜。」

text: When the year becomes cold, then we know how the pine and the cypress are the last to lose their leaves.
source: Analects 9:27 in Legge's numbering (tr. James Legge, 1893, public domain)
cjk: 子曰：「歲寒，然後知松柏之後彫也。」

text: Do not be desirous to have things done quickly; do not look at small advantages. Desire to have things done quickly prevents their being done thoroughly. Looking at small advantages prevents great affairs from being accomplished.
cjk: 子曰：「無欲速，無見小利。欲速則不達，見小利則大事不成。」

text: If a man take no thought about what is distant, he will find sorrow near at hand.
source: Analects 15:11 in Legge's numbering (tr. James Legge, 1893, public domain)
cjk: 子曰：「人無遠慮，必有近憂。」

text: Is there one word which may serve as a rule of practice for all one's life? — Is not reciprocity such a word? What you do not want done to yourself, do not do to others.
source: Analects 15:23 in Legge's numbering (tr. James Legge, 1893, public domain)
cjk: 子貢問曰：「有一言而可以終身行之者乎？」子曰：「其恕乎！己所不欲，勿施於人。」

text: To have faults and not to reform them, this, indeed, should be pronounced having faults.
source: Analects 15:29 in Legge's numbering (tr. James Legge, 1893, public domain)
cjk: 子曰：「過而不改，是謂過矣。」

text: By nature, men are nearly alike; by practice, they get to be wide apart.
cjk: 子曰：「性相近也，習相遠也。」

text: It's just my usual drug experiments...
Why am I taking a rumor so seriously? It's all just conjecture. But still... I guess I can take a quick peek.
The white face powder is poison. Don't let the baby touch it.
It truly is a sin to be ignorant.
I'm running a business here, sir, not a charity.
attribution: The Madam of the Verdigris House

text: I am of lowly birth. It must be a mistake.
Be careful out there. Kidnappings are on the rise.
Most poisons are only medicines that nobody bothered to weigh.
A rumour is a symptom. Find the fever behind it.
Taste everything twice: once to know it, once to be sure.
Grind slowly. The mortar does not care how important you are.
The rear palace runs on secrets; an apothecary runs on labels.
Do things out of love, not for love
